name: Media — advertising_agencies_producer_price_index covariate forecasting bundle (monthly)
citation: FRED (BLS PPI, Census retail, U. Michigan); Yahoo Finance via yfinance
license: FRED/BLS/Census/UMich public data (public domain / open); Yahoo Finance data for research use
description: Non-EIA, non-benchmark macro/equity signals; PPI advertising-services indices are BLS producer prices, not a common LLM forecasting-benchmark series, so not a contaminating training source. Long-format TempusBench bundle for application 'covariate_media_monthly_advertising_ppi'. Target 'advertising_agencies_producer_price_index' forecast from 5 covariates. monthly cadence, 117 timesteps, 2016-09-01..2026-05-01. NON-EIA (the foundation model is EIA-trained, so EIA sources are excluded). eia_derived=false.
preprocessing: 1. Pull FRED CSVs for PCU541810541810, PCU5152105152101, RSAFS, UMCSENT via fredgraph.csv (no key).
2. Parse observation_date + value; coerce '.' to NaN; index at first-of-month.
3. Download daily TTD and ^IXIC via yfinance (auto_adjust=True); take Close.
4. Resample each equity to monthly LAST valid close; re-stamp at month start (YYYY-MM-01).
5. Inner-join all six series on the month key over the common overlap (TTD IPO 2016-09 bounds left edge).
6. Linear-interpolate small internal gaps (<=3 consecutive); dropna to guarantee no NaN.
7. Add month_num from the date; order date,targets,covariates; write CSV + meta.json.
8. Reformatted wide->long TempusBench (variable_name, variable_unit, timestamps, values); timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; variable names expanded; missing->null; values round-trip-verified against source.
9. Removed calendar/time covariates (month_of_year) from the CSV so the only representation of time is the shared 'timestamps' column.

10. Variable names are written in plain English (underscores replaced with spaces). Target — 'advertising agencies producer price index' (from source column 'adagency_ppi', unit: index (1995-06=100)). Covariates — 'cable network advertising producer price index' (from source column 'cable_ad_ppi', unit: index); 'advance retail sales' (from source column 'retail_sales', unit: USD millions); 'university of michigan consumer sentiment' (from source column 'consumer_sentiment', unit: index); 'trade desk share price' (from source column 'ttd_close', unit: USD); 'nasdaq composite index' (from source column 'nasdaq_close', unit: index points).

11. Added binary calendar covariates 'is weekend', 'is holiday' (0/1), derived deterministically from the shared 'timestamps' (weekend = Sat/Sun; holiday = US federal holidays). This bundle is monthly (timestamps are month-start dates), so these day-level flags reflect only the 1st of each month and merely reflect the calendar status of that single first-of-month date, not the month as a whole (uninformative here).
12. Removed the calendar covariates 'is weekend' and 'is holiday' from the delivered CSV.
